title: Emergent modular Luttinger liquid from spin-partitioned entanglement in the one-dimensional Hubbard model
authors: Ádám Bácsi, Catalin Pascu Moca, Balázs Dóra
abstract: We study the spin-partitioned entanglement Hamiltonian of the one-dimensional repulsive Hubbard model. By combining bosonization with exact diagonalization, we show that tracing out one spin species produces a modular Luttinger liquid, whose properties fundamentally differ from those of the physical system. While the modular spectrum is fully dispersionless and possesses a momentum-independent entanglement gap, its eigenstates exhibit algebraic correlations governed by a single effective Luttinger parameter equal to the geometric mean of the charge and spin Luttinger parameters. The resulting entanglement spectrum displays a universal branching hierarchy in excellent agreement with exact diagonalization. We further demonstrate that the modular ground state is nearly identical to that of the spinless Luttinger liquid. These results uncover a universal modular structure in interacting one-dimensional fermionic systems.
summary: This work analyzes the entanglement structure of the 1D repulsive Hubbard model by examining the reduced density matrix after partitioning one spin species. The authors find that this leads to a modular Luttinger liquid whose correlations are governed by a single effective parameter, $\sqrt{K_c K_s}$. This demonstrates a universal principle: even when tracing out degrees of freedom, the entanglement structure retains critical algebraic correlations characteristic of 1D quantum liquids.
main_problem: The study aims to determine the universal low-energy entanglement Hamiltonian associated with a spin partition in an interacting one-dimensional metal, specifically investigating its structure when tracing out one spin species from the Hubbard model.
main_result: Tracing out one spin species yields a modular Luttinger liquid whose effective correlation is governed by a single parameter equal to the geometric mean of the charge and spin Luttinger parameters. This reveals a universal modular structure in 1D fermionic systems.
method: The authors combine bosonization techniques with exact diagonalization (ED) methods to calculate the reduced density matrix for one spin species, leading to the definition and analysis of an entanglement Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The primary system is the one-dimensional repulsive Hubbard model. The analysis proceeds by mapping the interacting fermionic problem onto bosonic fields via bosonization, allowing for the calculation of entanglement properties.
key_observables: Entanglement entropy, entanglement spectrum (eigenvalues of $H_{	ext{ent}}$), and Luttinger parameters ($K_c, K_s$).
important_parameters: The effective single LL parameter $\sqrt{K_c K_s}$, the repulsive interaction strength $U$, and the hopping amplitude $t$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on bosonization techniques and assumes that the reduced density matrix is Gaussian-structured, which is valid for the quadratic nature of the bosonized theory.
figures_summary: Figures visualize the universal branching hierarchy in the entanglement spectrum (Fig. 1) and show the evolution of the entanglement density of states compared to bosonization predictions (Fig. 2).
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical framework by defining the reduced density matrix for one spin species ($ho_\uparrow$) and deriving the associated entanglement Hamiltonian ($H_{	ext{mod}}$). It then applies this formalism to the Hubbard model, using bosonization results to predict universal properties like the effective Luttinger parameter and the branching structure of the spectrum.
why_interesting: The concept of an 'entanglement Hamiltonian' provides a powerful tool to characterize entanglement in interacting quantum systems. Finding that this modular structure is robust and yields a simple geometric mean for the correlation parameter offers deep insights into how entanglement encodes underlying symmetries, which is relevant for understanding exotic phases in correlated materials.
